title: Earthquake Safety & Drop, Cover, Hold On Guide
summary: During seismic activity, protect your head and torso immediately. Remember: DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON.
precautions: If indoors, DROP to your hands and knees, COVER your head and neck under a sturdy table or desk, and HOLD ON until shaking stops.
Stay away from glass windows, heavy furniture, hanging lights, and exterior walls.
If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings, streetlights, overhead wires, and trees.
If driving, pull over safely to a clear spot away from overpasses and bridges, and stay inside the vehicle.
Secure heavy appliances, tall shelves, and hanging objects to walls ahead of time.
evacuation: Do NOT use elevators. Always take the stairs after the shaking completely stops.
Check for structural damage, gas leaks, and electrical fires before exiting.
Evacuate calmly in an orderly line to designated open spaces, parks, or emergency assembly points.
Be prepared for aftershocks which can cause secondary structural collapses.
firstAid: Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth to stop heavy bleeding from debris wounds.
Immobilize suspected bone fractures using improvised splints before moving victims.
Clear dust or debris from victim's mouth and airway if they are struggling to breathe.
Do not move severely injured victims unless there is immediate danger of building collapse or fire.
emergencyChecklist: Sturdy shoes to protect feet from broken glass
First Aid Kit with bandages and antiseptics
dos: DO Drop, Cover, and Hold On during shaking.
DO protect your head with pillows or arms if no furniture is nearby.
DO turn off main gas valves if you smell gas after shaking stops.
DO stay calm and assist others nearby.
donts: DON'T run outside while the ground is actively shaking.
DON'T stand in doorways; sturdy desks or tables provide far better protection.
DON'T use elevators during or after an earthquake.
DON'T light matches or open flames in case of gas leaks.
